resources.string: Mechanism schematic · steps are conceptual, not a timeline
In this sample, leukocyte telomere length correlated with length in muscle, subcutaneous fat and skin (Pearson r = 0.83–0.84).
This cross-sectional comparison is not repeated measurement in the same person over time. Correlation does not make blood and tissue measurements interchangeable.
In blood T cells, log₂ p16(INK4a) mRNA expression correlated with chronological age (Pearson r = 0.63 across both cohorts).
This association does not count senescent cells in an organ or validate a personal aging test.
Cells detect and repair many DNA lesions. Persistent lesions and mutations are distinct outcomes that can disrupt normal cell function.

Telomeres protect chromosome ends. In many dividing cells they can shorten, and critically short ends can trigger a damage response. The response is not determined by a single length for every tissue.
Chromatin and chemical marks help govern which genes are active. Age-related changes in these marks can accompany altered gene expression without changing the underlying DNA sequence.
Chaperones and degradation systems help maintain functional proteins. If clearance cannot keep pace with damage, misfolded proteins may persist or aggregate.
Macroautophagy encloses some cytoplasmic material and delivers it to lysosomes. If delivery or degradation is impaired, cellular material may accumulate. The diagram shows the intact pathway.
Cells combine signals about nutrients and energy to coordinate growth and maintenance. Aging research examines changes in this regulation, not a diet or fasting target.
Mitochondria supply ATP and participate in stress signaling. Changes in their function and turnover can alter how cells meet energy demand and respond to stress.

Some stressed cells enter a durable arrest and can alter the signals they release. Senescence can play different roles in repair and chronic tissue changes; no single marker identifies every senescent cell.
Tissue stem cells renew themselves and produce descendants. Age-related changes in those cells and their surroundings can constrain renewal without implying that every stem cell is lost.
Cells coordinate tissue behavior with local and distant signals. Changes in the signal, its source or the receiving cell can modify a response without affecting all tissues in the same way.
Acute inflammation can support repair. Persistent inflammatory signaling is a separate research concern; a single inflammatory marker does not identify its cause or diagnose aging.

Gut microbial communities can change with age and influence interactions with the intestinal barrier. Diet, medicines and other factors also shape the community, so differences alone do not establish cause.
